Bhante, in 'web books meditations13 section0006 html 3ece61' (web books meditations13 section0006 html 3ece61), what is the core doctrinal teaching regarding 'When you focus your attention on'?

In this section from *web books meditations13 section0006 html 3ece61*, the master explains: *"When you focus your attention on the breath, you’re focusing on something that only you can know—how you feel the breathing from inside, how you feel your awareness from inside."*. From the perspective of the Four Noble Truths, suffering arises whenever the mind grasps at impermanent phenomena (*anicca*) as a reliable self (*atta*). By establishing clear comprehension (*sampajañña*) and seeing conditioned events as empty of inherent ownership, craving (*taṇhā*) is unhooked. It is like grasping a poisonous cobra by the tail: tempting and sleek from afar, but deadly the moment you grasp it. Release the tail and live in safety. Anchor your understanding in direct seeing rather than speculative theory.

Rest the mind gently in the rhythm of each natural in-and-out breath.
